entity.name: Abhijot Singh (Plexescor)
entity.description: 16-year-old self-taught systems developer from Hanumangarh, Rajasthan, India. Writing software since age 13, focused on native C++, Linux internals, and compiler design. Solo maintainer of HPR and the HPR extension ecosystem. Also building Tantrums, a compiled language with an LLVM backend.

projects.name: HPR Human Pattern Recorder
projects.description: A compiled, offline, zero-account activity tracker for Linux (Wayland/X11) and Windows. Built in C++23 with an 8-27MB RAM footprint, sandboxed Lua 5.4 extension engine with function overriding API, native browser and IDE project tracking without extensions, cross-day pattern analysis across 9 metrics, and a community extension registry called HPR Store. 450+ organic downloads across Linux and Windows in under 4 months. No telemetry by default, no cloud, no account required.

plans.name: HPR Round 1 Infrastructure and Ecosystem
plans.description: This is a one-time infrastructure and maintainer grant to support HPR's growth from a personal project into a properly sustained open source tool. I am currently hosting HPR on Netlify with the extension registry on GitHub Releases, both of which have real limitations as the project scales. This grant fixes that foundation and compensates me for active development time. Budget: monitor Rs 12000 (I need a second screen for my compilation workflow, I manually compile HPR and need a terminal and file manager visible simultaneously during builds), keyboard Rs 2200, mouse Rs 1000, Windows code signing certificate Rs 6500 (HPR's Windows installer currently triggers Microsoft SmartScreen on every install because it is unsigned, this scares away legitimate users and is a real adoption blocker I want to fix), Hostinger VPS 1 year Rs 5000 (to host HPR Store properly instead of GitHub Releases), hpr-cpp.dev domain Rs 2000, buffer for GST and bank fees Rs 1300, maintainer stipend Rs 10000 for active development and community support during the grant period. Total Rs 40000. Within 2 weeks I will migrate HPR website and docs to hpr-cpp.dev. Within 2 weeks I will publish a technical architecture blog post on FOSS United forum. Within 4 weeks I will integrate Windows code signing and eliminate SmartScreen warnings. Within 6 weeks I will grow HPR Store to 5+ extensions with contribution guidelines. Within 7 weeks I will ship 3 new first-party extensions.
